reels.caption:
HOME TOUR
When it came to designing our 1978 Ranch Style home we really wanted the space to not only reflect our personal style but also mirror the colors and the feeling of living in the desert.
Designing a space with that in mind has been a challenge that I have loved taking on.
We brought in so many special @potterybarn pieces that really brought our vision to life. Grounding elements like the Colton buffet that sits underneath my artwork pulls the dining area together.
One of my favorite projects has been the primary guest room. I wanted this room to have dark and moody furniture that beautifully contrasts the off white walls and floors, and the light colors of the desert landscape. I love the four post bed so much.
This room feels like a jump from what I have designed in the past and I love it.
As a woodworker I have had a lot of fun adding in different types wood and wood finishes into each room.
We have found inspiration in every aspect of desert life. Designing this home has been a dream so far and I am so happy to share this home tour!

@potterybarn Pieces in our home:
GREAT ROOM- Prism Rug, Colton Buffet, Andrea Dining Bench, Palisades Media Console, Palisades Console Desk, Heather/Chenille Jute Rug, Wall Mount Candleholder, Found Reclaimed Wood Candleholders, Aiken Jute Rug Runner
GUEST ROOM- Willow Four Poster Bed, Willow Nightstands, European Flax Linen Bedding, Frasier Vase Lamps, Montane Jute rug
BEDROOM- European Flax Linen Bedding, Melange Handcrafted Cotton Quilt, Cayman Platform Bed, Cayman Nightstands, Emery Linen Pinch Pleat Curtain, Paris Table Lamp. #hometour #interiordesign #desertlife

@am.irfatemi

Oasis project 🫐

This house is a modern desert settlement where architecture and nature merge. Brick volumes grow out of the natural rocks of the site, blurring boundaries and creating a native shelter that is true to the context.

It is a calm response to the desert landscape where brick forms have grown from the soil like natural masses. The design idea is based on connecting with the context and blurring the boundary between architecture and nature, where stone, brick, plants, and light transform the living space into a contemporary oasis.

It's not just about building a house — it's about rethinking what a container home can be. A visual idea meant to inspire new possibilities in modern housing.
